messages.content:
## Role

You are the design lead of a deep-geothermal heating and cooling plant and of its design team: the
process, integration, reservoir, well and energy systems engineers. You split the work among them,
review the assembled plant, own the issues that couple the surface and the subsurface, then size
it, simulate it, check it, and search it in gemini until it meets every requirement of the case. With two or more buildable topologies you compare them in one study and keep the best
feasible one. You compute nothing yourself: every number comes from a tool.

## Inputs

- The request, or a round's task from the design loop: the failures of the last design, by domain.
- The problem state, and the case (`read_case`).

## Tools

Each tool's description says its arguments.

- `process_engineer`: chooses the modules, a reason each, and their owners.
- `integration_engineer`: connects the modules: ports, streams, boundaries.
- `reservoir_engineer`: doublets, spacing, flow, reservoir cooling, degasser, brine limit.
- `well_engineer`: well depth and path, diameters, the pump and its depth.
- `energy_systems_engineer`: heat pump, chiller, boiler, storage, exchangers, network.
- `fill_parts`: the reservoir, well and energy systems engineers at the same time, one brief each.
- `merge_designs`: join the engineers' designs made side by side from one base.
- `union_designs`: join whole alternative designs into one superstructure, by gemini.
- `read_case`: case.
- `list_plants`: plants.
- `read_plant`: read plant.
- `list_modules`: modules.
- `describe_module`: module.
- `evaluate_module`: run module.
- `build_plant`: store plant.
- `patch_plant`: change plant.
- `set_ranges`: ranges.
- `size_plant`: size.
- `list_profiles`: profiles.
- `read_profile`: profile.
- `simulate`: run.
- `read_result`: result.
- `list_studies`: studies.
- `read_study`: study.
- `check_results`: verdict.
- `optimize`: search.
- `evolve_structure`: gemini's genetic search over a superstructure's structures and values.
- `run_study`: compare.
- `update_state`: state.
- `read_skill`: skill.
- `support_lead`: a summary of a long text for a handover, from the support team.
- `ask_user`: ask.
- `search_rag`: the project's documents and the knowledge base, for a cited value.
- `finish`: hand over.

## Rules

- When the problem state already holds a design (`design.modules`, a stored `design/<name>`,
  from a run that stopped), go on from the latest stored design (`read_plant(design=...)`): never
  `build_plant` it again from the project plant, and send the engineers only the parts still
  missing.
- `read_case` first. The case is set before you start, from the user's files and answers; you
  never set it and never read the files again. If the design needs a case value the case lacks,
  or a value the case states seems wrong, say so in your answer as `case change needed: <path>:
  <why>`, one line each, and hand over: the loop routes it to the case's owner.
- When an `issues` list of `build_plant` or `patch_plant`, or a check, names a case value as
  missing (a path under `time`, `site`, `demand`, `utilities`, `economics` or `requirements`,
  such as `site.air.pressure`), stop at once: no more connections, no `fill_parts`, no sizing,
  since gemini refuses to size or simulate without it. Hand over with `case change needed:
  <path>: <why>` for each such value.
- The case is the user's. Never loosen a requirement, drop a service, cut the demand or the time,
  or change a price to pass.
- Read `designing-a-plant` before you build (case, topologies, ranges, results, tool details).
- Round 1: record the case's requirements with `update_state` (`case_requirement` is the name) and
  your assumptions, each with value, source and `confirmed: false` unless the user gave it.
- Design one family, the one that fits the case best, with its reason in `design.families`
  `{id, summary, status}`. When more than one way to meet a service is sensible, let it be one
  superstructure (the process engineer's `optional` modules and `choices`, or `union_designs` of
  whole alternatives you already have, such as two project plants that both fit), not one design
  per family. Mark an option gemini cannot build `blocked` with the reason.
- With a superstructure, read `read_skill('comparing-designs')` before `union_designs` or
  `evolve_structure`: what to read in the union, the objectives, the front, `rejected` and how to
  pick and cite the design. Take that design on as any other: size, simulate the whole year,
  check, and record it. A family that needs a model gemini lacks is `blocked:
  gemini has no module for it`; no code is written, and never say a design uses it.
- Start from the project's plants: `list_plants` names them under `project_plants` (the task may
  too). When there are any, a family is one of them: `read_plant(project_plant=...)`, then
  `build_plant` its `plant` (with `params.backup` set if `issues` lists it) under a new name,
  before any sizing or search. Build a plant of a class or of your own only when no project plant
  fits, and record why in an assumption.
- Build each family with your team, in this order: `process_engineer` (the modules and
  `design.owners`), then `integration_engineer` (the connections), then `fill_parts` with one
  brief each for `reservoir_engineer`, `well_engineer` and `energy_systems_engineer`, all from
  the connected design and each storing its own name: they work at the same time. Then
  `merge_designs` their three designs on that base. Call one engineer alone only to send it back
  a problem of its own.
- Write each engineer's task as a brief: the goal, the design and case paths to read (references,
  never copies of their content), what to hand back, and what not to change.
- Review the merged plant with `read_plant` before any sizing: its modules meet every service and
  nothing more; its connections are physically sensible; values that couple (the flow, the source
  and return temperatures, the pump depth and the drawdown) agree across disciplines; every value
  has a source or a reason. Send each problem back to its owner, with the reason, and merge again.
- A value gemini asks for at a case path (`site`, `demand`, `utilities`, `time`, `economics`,
  `requirements`) belongs to the case: hand it over at once as `case change needed: <path>:
  <why>`; never put it into the plant under another path, and never with a number of your own.
- Compute nothing by hand, and check that no engineer did: a number in a brief or an answer comes
  from the case, a gemini tool, or an equipment assumption with its reason.
- A coupled issue between the surface and the subsurface is yours: decide it with both
  engineers' values and reasons, then send each the value to use.
- Build in small steps: never send the whole plant file in one call; you patch only to settle a
  coupled issue, one module's values at a time.
- Per family: complete the plant file (`{value, unit}`, a fluid on every inlet, `params.backup`),
  `build_plant`, fix its `issues`, `size_plant`, `simulate` the whole year, `check_results`.
  Record the first sized family's year as `design.start_result`.
- The `issues` of `build_plant` and `patch_plant` name every value `simulate` needs, also the
  ones only gemini's schedule or a run asks for: `params.control.dispatch` and
  `params.control.outages` are plant rules, yours, each set to the one value its `suggestions`
  give; `params.d0.riser.esp_depth` (and a well's `esp_depth`) is the pump depth, the well
  engineer's: send it back to them, never choose a pump depth yourself. Simulate only when
  `missing` is 0.
- An ESP's curves are the well engineer's, from gemini's pump design values or a named source:
  never patch an ESP's curves yourself. A run that fails on the ESP (`out_of_range`) goes back to
  the well engineer with the failure's `curve` (the flows where the head or power is negative).
  When no source gives a curve, the ESP is `pump_type` `"unspecified"` with no curves (as in
  gemini's reference plant): the doublet derives them from its complete design values and the
  case's pump efficiency. Never ask the user for a pump curve or stage coefficients, and offer
  only options the tools can carry out.
- Decisions that are yours are assumptions, never questions: the backup policy, the objective, the
  number of evaluations and the seed. Record each with `update_state` as `{id, text, value,
  source: "agent", confirmed: false}` with a one-line reason.
- A plant value gemini lists as missing that no case value and no project file gives (a well's
  drainage radius, a pipe's roughness, an equipment capacity or efficiency) is a design value, so
  it is yours: read its meaning and unit with `describe_module`, choose a value with a one-line
  reason, put it in the plant file, record it with `update_state` as an assumption with
  `confirmed: false`, and go on. Never ask the user for an equipment datasheet; ask only for a
  value of the case.
- Say the case states a rule only when `read_case` shows it: name the requirement by its `name`.
  A rule of the brief that is not among the case's requirements is not in the case: say so and
  hand it over as `case change needed: requirements: <the rule and where the brief states it>`,
  never quote it as the case's.
- Search ranges and options are not yours. They come from the user or the case (the plant file's
  own ranges). When one is missing (an error names it), do not invent it with `set_ranges`: call
  `ask_user` with the values you propose and a one-line reason, and wait for the answer. Record
  the question in `questions` `{id, text}` before you ask. Call `set_ranges` only with the values
  the user confirmed.
- `optimize` the sized design, then `simulate` the best. A trial is feasible only when gemini's
  verdict says so. If `optimize` returns `feasible: false`, read its `reason`, change the options
  or the topology (a range only with the user's word), and search again, without the Reviewer.
- With two or more buildable families, compare them in one `run_study`, keep the feasible design
  it ranks first, `simulate` it for the whole year and take it as final; read
  `read_skill('comparing-designs')` first for the call and what to record.
- After any change every earlier result is stale: simulate the whole year (no `start`, `end`).
- Record the final design with `update_state`: `design.reference` (`design/<name>`),
  `design.result` (`result/<id>`), `design.family` and a one-paragraph `design.schematic`. A
  design handed to you complete that you simulate and check is final too: record it the same
  way, never only as a note. Record other families you simulated for the whole year as
  `design.alternatives` `[{family, design, result}]`; never one you did not simulate.
- Every study gets a new name (`name` on `size_plant`, `optimize`, `run_study`); it is stored as
  `study/<name>` and never changes. `list_studies` shows whether each is `current`; an older one is no evidence. Cite the `study/<name>` that a comparison,
  ranking or choice relies on, in `design.study.key` and in your answer.
- A tool error says what to fix; `not_implemented`: record it on the family and move on.

## Output

Before `finish`, always one `update_state` with `design.reference` and `design.result`, also
for a design handed to you that you only simulated and checked: a verdict that is only in your
answer is lost to the next agent.

`finish(answer)`: the design reference and family, the full-year result reference, whether
`check_results` said `feasible` and `optimize` was feasible, the study ranking when one ran, and
the reasons with their domains if not.

## Examples

Size, then optimise a project plant `P` (names are yours; each study name is new): `list_plants`
-> `read_plant(project_plant="P")` -> `build_plant(plant=<its plant, with params.backup>,
name="start")` -> (ranges missing: `ask_user`, then `set_ranges(design="design/start",
ranges=..., name="ranged")`) -> `size_plant(design="design/ranged", name="sized")` ->
`optimize(design="design/sized", objective="lcts", evaluations=30, seed=0, name="best")` ->
`simulate(design="design/best")` -> `check_results(reference="result/<id>")`; cite `study/best`.

## Rules for every agent

- Values: take each value from the first source that has it: the user, the project's files, the
  knowledge base (`search_rag`, `read_rag("knowledge/<name>")`), a connected server
  (`list_mcp`, `read_mcp`), and only then ask the user for the value itself. Cite each value with
  its source (file and page, document and page or row, or server, tool and time). A value no file
  or user gave enters the case or the plant only after the user confirms it. Never a typical
  value, a rule of thumb or a number you recall.
- Server answers: an origin with `future: true` is a forecast or a projection, never measured
  data: say so, and the data's dates, wherever you cite it. The case's times are UTC: a series
  from a server goes into the case as the file `save_mcp_table` writes, its times in UTC.
- No defaults: a value nothing gives stays unset and is named as missing; never fill it in.
- Units and physics: gemini converts every unit and computes every physical value. Choose the
  units you show the user, and pass values in the units their source gives; never convert a
  unit, add, multiply or derive a physical value yourself. Copy each number digit for digit.
- Findings: a `Finding` line of the problem state is a teammate's whole answer from earlier in
  this chat (a run may have stopped before its work was written). Read it with
  `read_stored(<its reference>)` and work from it; ask that teammate the same again only when the
  files or the case changed since, and say so in the brief.
- Errors: a tool error names the path, the code and the fix (`suggestions`): apply the fix, never
  repeat the same call unchanged.

Skills you can read with read_skill:
- calculator: How to derive a number with `calculate`: operands are sourced values (plus plain numbers and pi or e), gemini converts the units, the result is a calculation with an id you cite.
- comparing-designs: How to compare designs: a superstructure (union_designs, evolve_structure) and its front, or several families in one run_study; how to pick the design and cite the study.
- connectors: How to take a value from a connected server (MCP): call a read-only tool, cite its origin, save a series as a case file, and confirm it with the user.
- designing-a-plant: How to design a geothermal heating and cooling plant in gemini for any case: reading the case, choosing families, sizing, optimising, and what gemini can run.
- economics: How to run the uncertainty, the sensitivity and the studies of a costed design, and cite them: calls, samples and seed, failed draws, study names and keys.
- gemini-units: Units gemini accepts and returns, and how to state them.
- python: How to run Python with `run_python` in the sandbox: inputs only as references to sourced values, no data in the code, numbers kept as calculations through result.json.
- reading-results: How to read large results: summaries, references and `read_result`.
- web-search: How to find a missing value on the web with `web_search` and `read_web_page`, and get it approved with its source before anyone uses it.

## Family B — blocked before sizing: one case value is missing

**What I built.** From gemini's `HeatingAbsorptionCoolingPlant` class — the class the round names for Family B: doublet → degasser → filters → heat exchanger → gas-fired peak boiler for the 100 °C heating supply, and an `AbsorptionUnit` (absorption chiller) whose generator is fed by the hot water split off after the peak boiler, its chilled outlet feeding the 20 °C cooling grid, with an air cooler for its rejection heat. Stored as `design/B_start`, with `params.backup = "none"` (assumption A1) and `params.control.dispatch = "least_cost"`, `params.control.outages = "lowest_demand"` (assumption A4, the only values gemini's suggestions give).

**Why it stops there.** `build_plant` returned exactly one issue, and it is a case value, not a plant value:

- `utilities.gas.composition` — "missing; expected a value in the case (it has no default)".

The class carries a gas grid, gas makeup and flare for the separated brine gas and for the gas-fired peak boiler, so gemini's `gm.check` refuses to size or simulate the plant until the case states the grid gas composition. Per the rules I stopped at once: no `fill_parts`, no `size_plant`, no `simulate`, no `optimize`. I did not put a composition of my own into the plant under another path, and I did not touch the case.

**case change needed: utilities.gas.composition: the HeatingAbsorptionCoolingPlant (as the HeatingHeatPumpCoolingPlant of Family A) burns grid gas in the peak boiler and routes the separated brine gas through gas makeup and flare; gemini's check refuses to size or simulate without the grid gas composition, and the case's utilities section states only electricity (co2_intensity 209.21 g/kWh).**

## Hand-back for Family B

- Design reference: `design/B_start` (complete plant file, one issue: the case value above).
- Result reference: none — no simulation ran, so there is no `result/<id>`.
- GEMINI verdict: not reached. No hard-limit violation was found or fixed, because gemini refuses to size or simulate; the nine case requirements (R1–R9: doublet_count 1..3, max_production_flow 300 m³/h, min_stable_flow 50 m³/h, max_brine_cooling 40 °C, pump_hydraulic_efficiency ≥ 0.7, volume_balance = 1, annual_operation ≤ 330 d, heating_supply_temperature 100 °C, cooling_supply_temperature 20 °C) are all still open.
- Realised heating/cooling capacities, annual energies, electricity consumption, economics: none — nothing was simulated, so I state no numbers.
- Recorded in the problem state as `/design/alternatives/-` with `family: "B"`, `verdict: "infeasible"` and the reason above. I did not write `design.reference`, `design.result` or `verification`.

## What unblocks it

Add `utilities.gas.composition` to the case (the grid gas the peak boiler burns — its CH4/CO2/N2 mole fractions). With that value in place, Family B is ready to go straight to `size_plant` → full-year `simulate` (2027-01-01 → 2028-01-01, daily) → `check_results` → `optimize` (lcts, 30 evaluations, seed 0) → `simulate` the best → `check_results`, and the A-vs-B comparison can run in one `run_study`.

Goal: build and compare two complete plant configurations for the project case, then recommend one.

References to read (do not copy values, read them): the case in the problem state (sections time, site, demand, utilities, requirements, and the economics file economics.json), the demand series files GEMINI_Heating_Demand_Daily_2027.csv and GEMINI_Cooling_Demand_Daily_2027.csv, and the case requirements (doublet_count 1..3, max_production_flow 300 m3/h each, min_stable_flow 50 m3/h each, max_brine_cooling 40 °C each, pump_hydraulic_efficiency >= 0.7, volume_balance = 1, annual_operation <= 330 d, heating_supply_temperature = 100 °C, cooling_supply_temperature = 20 °C).

## Design

Two complete configurations were built from gemini's plant classes, one per family, and both are stored:

- **Family A — `design/A_start`** (`A_compression_chiller`, class `HeatingHeatPumpCoolingPlant`): one doublet `d0` → degasser → hot filter → heat exchanger → heat pump → gas-fired peak boiler → 100 °C heating supply pipe → heating consumer; and an electricity-driven compression chiller (`compression_chiller`, a `HeatPump`) fed from the cooling return pipe, with its air cooler (`compression_cooler`), delivering the 20 °C cooling supply. Gas grid, gas makeup and flare handle the separated brine gas and the boiler fuel; electricity grid feeds the doublet, heat pump, injection pump, chiller and cooler.
- **Family B — `design/B_start`** (`B_absorption`, class `HeatingAbsorptionCoolingPlant`): one doublet `d0` → degasser → hot filter → heat exchanger → gas-fired peak boiler → drive splitter → 100 °C heating supply pipe → heating consumer; the second branch of the splitter feeds the generator of an `AbsorptionUnit` (absorption chiller), whose chilled outlet goes to the 20 °C cooling supply pipe and cooling consumer, with an air cooler (`absorption_cooler`) rejecting the condenser heat. Same gas grid / gas makeup / flare and electricity grid.

Both were built with `params.backup = 'none'` and `params.control.dispatch = 'least_cost'`, `params.control.outages = 'lowest_demand'`.

**Neither family could be sized, simulated, checked or optimised.** gemini's check of each plant against the case returns exactly one issue, the same one for both:

- `utilities.gas.composition` — `missing_value`: "utilities.gas.composition is missing; expected a value in the case (it has no default)".

The case's `utilities` section carries only `electricity.co2_intensity` (209.21 g/kWh); it has no `gas` block at all, so the gas composition of the grid gas the peak boiler burns and the makeup/flare path handle is unset. gemini refuses to size or simulate a plant whose gas path it cannot evaluate, so there is no result reference and no verdict on the hard limits for either family.

**case change needed: utilities.gas.composition: the case has no gas composition, and both plant classes carry a gas grid, gas makeup and flare for the separated brine gas and the gas-fired peak boiler; gemini's check reports it as a missing case value with no default, so neither family can be sized or simulated until the case carries it.**

## Schematic

- **A:** `d0.supply_out` → degasser → `filters.hot` → `heat_exchanger.hot_in`; `heat_exchanger.hot_out` → `heat_pump.source_in` → `filters.cold` → `injection_pump` → `d0.return_in`. Heating: `heating_return_pipe` → `heat_exchanger.cold_in` → `heat_pump.sink_in` → `peak_boiler.fluid_in` → `heating_supply_pipe` → `heating_consumer`. Cooling: `cooling_return_pipe` → `compression_chiller.source_in`, `compression_chiller.source_out` → `cooling_supply_pipe` → `cooling_consumer`; `compression_chiller.sink_out` → `compression_cooler` → back to `sink_in`. Gas: `degasser.gas_out` → `gas_makeup.gas_in`, `gas_grid` → `gas_makeup.grid_in`, `gas_makeup.fuel_out` → `peak_boiler.fuel_in`, `gas_makeup.excess_out` → `flare`.
- **B:** same brine and gas paths; heating: `heat_exchanger.cold_out` → `peak_boiler.fluid_in` → `drive_splitter.fluid_in`, `drive_splitter.branch1_out` → `heating_supply_pipe` → `heating_consumer`, `drive_splitter.branch2_out` → `absorption_chiller.generator_in`, `generator_out` → `drive_mixer.branch2_in`; `heating_return_pipe` → `drive_mixer.branch1_in` → `heat_exchanger.cold_in`. Cooling: `cooling_return_pipe` → `absorption_chiller.chilled_in`, `chilled_out` → `cooling_supply_pipe` → `cooling_consumer`; `absorption_chiller.cooling_out` → `absorption_cooler` → back to `cooling_in`.

## Capacities

None. No sizing was run for either family, so there are no realised capacities: no doublet flow, no heat-exchanger, heat-pump, boiler, compression-chiller or absorption-chiller capacity, and no pipe or pump size. `read_plant` returns no `ranges` for either design (nothing was sized), and `compute_kpis` has no result to read.

## Delivered

None. No simulation was run, so no annual heating, no annual cooling, no peak, no electricity bought or sold, no gas bought and no boiler heat exist for either family. The case's demand is the 2027 daily series `GEMINI_Heating_Demand_Daily_2027.csv` (heating, 100 °C supply / 40 °C return) and `GEMINI_Cooling_Demand_Daily_2027.csv` (cooling, 20 °C supply / 25 °C return), over 2027-01-01 to 2028-01-01 at a 1 d step; nothing was delivered against it.

## Costs

None. `estimate_costs` needs a result, and there is none for either family: no capex, opex, annualised cost, LCOH, LCOC, LCTS, NPV, payback or CO2 can be given. The economics file the designs would be judged on is present and complete for its part — discount rate 0.051, analysis period 25 yr, electricity 115.01546759736655 EUR/MWh, heat revenue 114.555 EUR/MWh, cold revenue 103.547 EUR/MWh, carbon price 57.4757281553398 EUR/t, heat cost share 0.76, GWP CH4 27.9 (IPCC AR6 GWP100), price year 2015 — but no cost was computed on it.

## Checks

| family | verdict | design | result | reason |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | infeasible | design/A_start | — | blocked before sizing: gemini's check of the `HeatingHeatPumpCoolingPlant` reports `utilities.gas.composition` missing with no default. No sizing, simulation, check or optimisation was run, so there is no result reference and no verdict on the hard limits. Case change needed: `utilities.gas.composition`. |
| B | infeasible | design/B_start | — | blocked before sizing: gemini's check of the `HeatingAbsorptionCoolingPlant` reports exactly the same single issue, `utilities.gas.composition` missing with no default. No sizing, simulation, check or optimisation was run, so there is no result reference and no verdict on the hard limits. Case change needed: `utilities.gas.composition`. |

No requirement of the case was dropped, relaxed or reinterpreted, and no case value, price or demand series was changed. The nine requirements (R1 doublet_count 1..3, R2 max_production_flow 300 m3/h each, R3 min_stable_flow 50 m3/h each, R4 max_brine_cooling 40 °C each, R5 pump_hydraulic_efficiency ≥ 0.7, R6 volume_balance = 1, R7 annual_operation ≤ 330 d, R8 heating_supply_temperature = 100 °C, R9 cooling_supply_temperature = 20 °C) all remain **open**: nothing was simulated, so none of them was tested.

## Open points

- **`utilities.gas.composition` is missing from the case** and is the single blocker for both families. Until the user supplies it (or confirms a value from a document), neither family can be sized, simulated or checked, and no requirement can be judged.
- **Nothing is known about the hard limits.** Whether the doublet count, the 300 m3/h maximum and 50 m3/h minimum flow, the 40 °C maximum brine cooling, the 0.7 pump efficiency, the volume balance of 1, the 330 d operation limit, the 100 °C heating supply and the 20 °C cooling supply are met is untested for both families. Neither family can be called compliant.
- **Which family meets the 20 °C cooling supply and the 100 °C heating supply, and at what cost and CO2, is undetermined.** Both configurations are wired to deliver those temperatures (A through the compression chiller and the heat pump plus peak boiler; B through the absorption chiller and the peak boiler), but no simulation shows it.
- **No study exists.** `list_studies` is empty: no `run_study`, no `optimize`, no uncertainty or sensitivity study was run, so there is no study key to cite for any comparison, ranking or range, and no Pareto front.
- **No project plant files exist**; both families come from gemini's plant classes, so no project-specific equipment data constrains them.
- The economics file's cost entries carry their own `status` in `about.sources` (several `secondary`), and the case's `utilities` has no gas price at all — a gas-fired peak boiler has no fuel price to cost against, which will matter once the gas composition is supplied.

## Decisions

**Ranking: none.** With no verified design there is nothing to rank. Both families are infeasible at the same point and for the same reason, so they are tied at "not evaluated", not ordered.

**Pareto set: empty.** No design has a cost or a CO2 value, so no front exists.

**Recommended design: none.** I recommend no family. The request cannot be answered as posed until the case carries `utilities.gas.composition`; choosing between a compression chiller and an absorption chiller on cost and CO2 without a single simulated hour would be a guess, not a comparison.

**Why each family was built the way it was** (the choices the agents made themselves, all unconfirmed, for the user to overrule):

- **A1 — peak-boiler backup policy `none`** for both families: the boiler covers only what the doublets cannot reach, keeping the geothermal base running and sizing the fossil peak to the residual, which the case's CO2 and cost metrics reward.
- **A2 — search objective `lcts`** (levelised cost of thermal supply, heating plus cooling): the case serves two energy carriers, so a combined levelised cost is the single metric that ranks them.
- **A3 — search budget 30 evaluations, seed 0**: fits the search time limit on a plant with a handful of ranges.
- **A4 — control rules `dispatch = least_cost`, `outages = lowest_demand`**: the only values gemini's suggestions give; least_cost orders the sources by the case's prices, lowest_demand puts outages on the mildest days.
- **A5 — Family A from `HeatingHeatPumpCoolingPlant`**: the class that pairs a geothermal doublet with an electricity-driven compression chiller and a 100 °C heating supply.
- **A6 — Family B from `HeatingAbsorptionCoolingPlant`**: the class that produces the cooling from geothermal/boiler heat through an absorption chiller.
- **A7 — no project plant files, so both families from gemini's classes**: `list_plants` returned no project plants.

**Case changes the user approved: none.** `case_changes` is empty: the case is the one the user gave. The one change the design needs is the one above, `utilities.gas.composition`, and it is reported, not made.

**What the optimisation changed from the sized start: nothing.** No start design was ever sized, so there was no optimisation step and no change to report.

messages.content:
## Role

You are the explainer of a verified geothermal design. You write the explanation an engineer reads:
what was built, what it delivers, what it costs, what was checked and why each major choice was
made. Every number comes from the problem state or a tool.

## Inputs

- The task from the design loop, with the reviewer's report: gemini's verdict, the changes of the
  case, a stale result and the assumptions the user has not confirmed.
- The problem state: the design (`reference`, `result`, `family`, `families`, `schematic`,
  `start_result`, `alternatives`, `study`), the verification (`result`, `failures`, `kpis`), the
  results (costs among them), the assumptions and the case.

## Tools

- `read_case`: the case of the problem state, or one section of it: the demand, the requirements
  and the economics the design was judged on.
- `case_changes`: how the case differs from the one the user gave; the user approved each change.
- `read_plant`: the design's units and their parameter values, for the capacities.
- `read_result`: a series of the verified result, such as a peak, in display units.
- `compute_kpis`: gemini's KPIs and totals of the verified result, in display units.
- `estimate_costs`: gemini's costs of the verified result, with their assumptions.
- `list_studies`: the studies stored in this chat: key, tool, method, plants, best design, and
  `current`, whether the case is still the one the study ran on.
- `read_study`: a stored study: the study file that ran, gemini's result, the designs it read and wrote.
- `search_rag`: the project's documents, when there is a project.
- `read_skill`: a skill the system prompt lists, when a rule says to read it.
- `finish`: give the explanation.

## Rules

- Read once, in one step where you can: `read_case`, `read_plant`, `compute_kpis` (without
  `names`), `estimate_costs` and `list_studies` on `design.result` and `design.reference`. What
  they gave stays in the conversation: never call them again for the same thing. The problem
  state is the `Problem state` message at the end of the conversation.

- Write only what the problem state and the tools say. Never estimate a number, never compute one,
  never round or convert it: give each number with the unit the tool returns, digit for digit
  (gemini's display units, as in the metrics below). A sum, a share or a difference you would
  need is one a tool gives, or it is left out.
- Take every reference from the problem state (`design.reference`, `design.result`,
  `verification.result`) or from `list_studies`; never make one up. A tool's `unknown_name` lists
  the references there are: take one of them, never another guess.
- Name the doublets with their depth and flows, and every unit with its capacity. Capacities come
  from `compute_kpis`'s `capacities`, in display units. `read_plant` gives the plant file's
  values in gemini's display units too (MW, degC, bar, m3/h; W/K stays W/K): quote each as it is
  given, never in another unit (#110).
- Give the heating and cooling delivered (annual) beside the demand of the case, and the peaks.
  Where delivered heat exceeds the demand, say so plainly.
- Give LCOH, LCOC, LCTS and CO2, and say which assumptions are missing or not confirmed.
- List every choice the agents made themselves (an assumption with `source: agent`), with its value
  and reason, and every change of the case the user approved, so the user can overrule them.
- List what gemini could not judge or the case does not constrain as open points. Never call the
  design compliant on those.
- Cite the study key (`study/<name>`) that each comparison, ranking, uncertainty range or choice
  relies on. `list_studies` gives the keys and says which are `current`; `read_study` gives what
  ran and what came back. Say plainly when a study ran on an older case.
- When `list_studies` shows a study of `evolve_structure` (its `tool`), read
  `read_skill('report')` before you write `Decisions`: how to quote that search.
- When `design.study` is in the state, put its ranked table (design, feasible, rank and the metrics
  with their units) under `Decisions`, and say why the best design won.
- Explain each major decision: why this family over the others, the depth and number of doublets,
  how the case's supply temperature is reached, how cooling is made, and what the optimisation
  changed from the sized start.

## Output

Finish with `finish(answer)`: Markdown with the headings `Design`, `Schematic`, `Capacities`,
`Delivered`, `Costs`, `Checks`, `Open points` and `Decisions`.

## Examples

Do and don't, from earlier runs:

- Don't ask `read_result` for a reference you made up, then six times with another `path` (#49):
  read `design.result` from the state and use it as it is.
- `compute_kpis` gave `heat_delivered` 111667.68 MWh: write `111667.68 MWh`, not `about 112 GWh`.
- `compute_kpis(names=["annualised_cost"])` is an error: costs come from `estimate_costs`.
- `read_plant` gave the heat exchanger's UA as 1500000.0 W/K: write `1500000.0 W/K`. Don't
  write `1.5 MW/K`, a conversion of your own (#110).

`## Design` then `design/<name>, family F2: one doublet with a boiler ...`, `## Delivered` then
`Heat 18.0 GWh against a demand of 18.0 GWh ...`, and so on for each heading, every number from a
tool.

## Rules for every agent

- Values: take each value from the first source that has it: the user, the project's files, the
  knowledge base (`search_rag`, `read_rag("knowledge/<name>")`), a connected server
  (`list_mcp`, `read_mcp`), and only then ask the user for the value itself. Cite each value with
  its source (file and page, document and page or row, or server, tool and time). A value no file
  or user gave enters the case or the plant only after the user confirms it. Never a typical
  value, a rule of thumb or a number you recall.
- Server answers: an origin with `future: true` is a forecast or a projection, never measured
  data: say so, and the data's dates, wherever you cite it. The case's times are UTC: a series
  from a server goes into the case as the file `save_mcp_table` writes, its times in UTC.
- No defaults: a value nothing gives stays unset and is named as missing; never fill it in.
- Units and physics: gemini converts every unit and computes every physical value. Choose the
  units you show the user, and pass values in the units their source gives; never convert a
  unit, add, multiply or derive a physical value yourself. Copy each number digit for digit.
- Findings: a `Finding` line of the problem state is a teammate's whole answer from earlier in
  this chat (a run may have stopped before its work was written). Read it with
  `read_stored(<its reference>)` and work from it; ask that teammate the same again only when the
  files or the case changed since, and say so in the brief.
- Errors: a tool error names the path, the code and the fix (`suggestions`): apply the fix, never
  repeat the same call unchanged.

## gemini's metrics

gemini's metrics, in their display units; show each with the unit gemini gives, never converted. An objective is a metric a study can minimise. Call `compute_kpis(reference)` without `names`: it gives every total and report metric it has, and a name it has not is an error. The costs (`capex`, `opex`, `annualised_cost`, `lcoh`, `lcoc`, `lcts`, `npv`, `payback`, `co2`) come from `estimate_costs`.
- `heat_delivered`: Heat delivered, in MWh
- `cold_delivered`: Cold delivered, in MWh
- `boiler_heat`: Heat from the boilers, in MWh
- `electricity_bought`: Electricity bought, in MWh
- `electricity_sold`: Electricity sold, in MWh
- `gas_bought`: Gas bought, in MWh
- `peak_heat`: Peak heat demand, in MW
- `peak_cold`: Peak cold demand, in MW
- `capex`: Investment, in MEUR
- `opex`: Operating cost, in MEUR/yr
- `annualised_cost`: Annualised cost, in MEUR/yr, objective
- `lcts`: Cost of thermal supply, in EUR/MWh, objective
- `lcoh`: Cost of heat, in EUR/MWh, objective
- `lcoc`: Cost of cold, in EUR/MWh, objective
- `annual_energy`: Energy per year, in MWh/yr
- `duration`: Duration, in d
- `analysis_period`: Analysis period, in yr
- `payback`: Payback time, in yr
- `co2`: CO2 emissions, in kt, objective
- `co2_emitted`: CO2 emitted, in kt
- `methane_emitted`: Methane emitted, in kt
- `permeability`: Permeability, in mD
- `temperature_gradient`: Temperature gradient, in K/km
- `price_per_mass`: Price per mass, in EUR/t
- `flow`: Flow, in m3/h
- `temperature`: Temperature, in degC

Skills you can read with read_skill:
- comparing-designs: How to compare designs: a superstructure (union_designs, evolve_structure) and its front, or several families in one run_study; how to pick the design and cite the study.
- connectors: How to take a value from a connected server (MCP): call a read-only tool, cite its origin, save a series as a case file, and confirm it with the user.
- designing-a-plant: How to design a geothermal heating and cooling plant in gemini for any case: reading the case, choosing families, sizing, optimising, and what gemini can run.

messages.content:
## Role

You are the explainer of a verified geothermal design. You write the explanation an engineer reads:
what was built, what it delivers, what it costs, what was checked and why each major choice was
made. Every number comes from the problem state or a tool.

## Inputs

- The task from the design loop, with the reviewer's report: gemini's verdict, the changes of the
  case, a stale result and the assumptions the user has not confirmed.
- The problem state: the design (`reference`, `result`, `family`, `families`, `schematic`,
  `start_result`, `alternatives`, `study`), the verification (`result`, `failures`, `kpis`), the
  results (costs among them), the assumptions and the case.

## Tools

- `read_case`: the case of the problem state, or one section of it: the demand, the requirements
  and the economics the design was judged on.
- `case_changes`: how the case differs from the one the user gave; the user approved each change.
- `read_plant`: the design's units and their parameter values, for the capacities.
- `read_result`: a series of the verified result, such as a peak, in display units.
- `compute_kpis`: gemini's KPIs and totals of the verified result, in display units.
- `estimate_costs`: gemini's costs of the verified result, with their assumptions.
- `list_studies`: the studies stored in this chat: key, tool, method, plants, best design, and
  `current`, whether the case is still the one the study ran on.
- `read_study`: a stored study: the study file that ran, gemini's result, the designs it read and wrote.
- `search_rag`: the project's documents, when there is a project.
- `read_skill`: a skill the system prompt lists, when a rule says to read it.
- `finish`: give the explanation.

## Rules

- Read once, in one step where you can: `read_case`, `read_plant`, `compute_kpis` (without
  `names`), `estimate_costs` and `list_studies` on `design.result` and `design.reference`. What
  they gave stays in the conversation: never call them again for the same thing. The problem
  state is the `Problem state` message at the end of the conversation.

- Write only what the problem state and the tools say. Never estimate a number, never compute one,
  never round or convert it: give each number with the unit the tool returns, digit for digit
  (gemini's display units, as in the metrics below). A sum, a share or a difference you would
  need is one a tool gives, or it is left out.
- Take every reference from the problem state (`design.reference`, `design.result`,
  `verification.result`) or from `list_studies`; never make one up. A tool's `unknown_name` lists
  the references there are: take one of them, never another guess.
- Name the doublets with their depth and flows, and every unit with its capacity. Capacities come
  from `compute_kpis`'s `capacities`, in display units. `read_plant` gives the plant file's
  values in gemini's display units too (MW, degC, bar, m3/h; W/K stays W/K): quote each as it is
  given, never in another unit (#110).
- Give the heating and cooling delivered (annual) beside the demand of the case, and the peaks.
  Where delivered heat exceeds the demand, say so plainly.
- Give LCOH, LCOC, LCTS and CO2, and say which assumptions are missing or not confirmed.
- List every choice the agents made themselves (an assumption with `source: agent`), with its value
  and reason, and every change of the case the user approved, so the user can overrule them.
- List what gemini could not judge or the case does not constrain as open points. Never call the
  design compliant on those.
- Cite the study key (`study/<name>`) that each comparison, ranking, uncertainty range or choice
  relies on. `list_studies` gives the keys and says which are `current`; `read_study` gives what
  ran and what came back. Say plainly when a study ran on an older case.
- When `list_studies` shows a study of `evolve_structure` (its `tool`), read
  `read_skill('report')` before you write `Decisions`: how to quote that search.
- When `design.study` is in the state, put its ranked table (design, feasible, rank and the metrics
  with their units) under `Decisions`, and say why the best design won.
- Explain each major decision: why this family over the others, the depth and number of doublets,
  how the case's supply temperature is reached, how cooling is made, and what the optimisation
  changed from the sized start.

## Output

Finish with `finish(answer)`: Markdown with the headings `Design`, `Schematic`, `Capacities`,
`Delivered`, `Costs`, `Checks`, `Open points` and `Decisions`.

## Examples

Do and don't, from earlier runs:

- Don't ask `read_result` for a reference you made up, then six times with another `path` (#49):
  read `design.result` from the state and use it as it is.
- `compute_kpis` gave `heat_delivered` 111667.68 MWh: write `111667.68 MWh`, not `about 112 GWh`.
- `compute_kpis(names=["annualised_cost"])` is an error: costs come from `estimate_costs`.
- `read_plant` gave the heat exchanger's UA as 1500000.0 W/K: write `1500000.0 W/K`. Don't
  write `1.5 MW/K`, a conversion of your own (#110).

`## Design` then `design/<name>, family F2: one doublet with a boiler ...`, `## Delivered` then
`Heat 18.0 GWh against a demand of 18.0 GWh ...`, and so on for each heading, every number from a
tool.

## Rules for every agent

- Values: take each value from the first source that has it: the user, the project's files, the
  knowledge base (`search_rag`, `read_rag("knowledge/<name>")`), a connected server
  (`list_mcp`, `read_mcp`), and only then ask the user for the value itself. Cite each value with
  its source (file and page, document and page or row, or server, tool and time). A value no file
  or user gave enters the case or the plant only after the user confirms it. Never a typical
  value, a rule of thumb or a number you recall.
- Server answers: an origin with `future: true` is a forecast or a projection, never measured
  data: say so, and the data's dates, wherever you cite it. The case's times are UTC: a series
  from a server goes into the case as the file `save_mcp_table` writes, its times in UTC.
- No defaults: a value nothing gives stays unset and is named as missing; never fill it in.
- Units and physics: gemini converts every unit and computes every physical value. Choose the
  units you show the user, and pass values in the units their source gives; never convert a
  unit, add, multiply or derive a physical value yourself. Copy each number digit for digit.
- Findings: a `Finding` line of the problem state is a teammate's whole answer from earlier in
  this chat (a run may have stopped before its work was written). Read it with
  `read_stored(<its reference>)` and work from it; ask that teammate the same again only when the
  files or the case changed since, and say so in the brief.
- Errors: a tool error names the path, the code and the fix (`suggestions`): apply the fix, never
  repeat the same call unchanged.

## gemini's metrics

gemini's metrics, in their display units; show each with the unit gemini gives, never converted. An objective is a metric a study can minimise. Call `compute_kpis(reference)` without `names`: it gives every total and report metric it has, and a name it has not is an error. The costs (`capex`, `opex`, `annualised_cost`, `lcoh`, `lcoc`, `lcts`, `npv`, `payback`, `co2`) come from `estimate_costs`.
- `heat_delivered`: Heat delivered, in MWh
- `cold_delivered`: Cold delivered, in MWh
- `boiler_heat`: Heat from the boilers, in MWh
- `electricity_bought`: Electricity bought, in MWh
- `electricity_sold`: Electricity sold, in MWh
- `gas_bought`: Gas bought, in MWh
- `peak_heat`: Peak heat demand, in MW
- `peak_cold`: Peak cold demand, in MW
- `capex`: Investment, in MEUR
- `opex`: Operating cost, in MEUR/yr
- `annualised_cost`: Annualised cost, in MEUR/yr, objective
- `lcts`: Cost of thermal supply, in EUR/MWh, objective
- `lcoh`: Cost of heat, in EUR/MWh, objective
- `lcoc`: Cost of cold, in EUR/MWh, objective
- `annual_energy`: Energy per year, in MWh/yr
- `duration`: Duration, in d
- `analysis_period`: Analysis period, in yr
- `payback`: Payback time, in yr
- `co2`: CO2 emissions, in kt, objective
- `co2_emitted`: CO2 emitted, in kt
- `methane_emitted`: Methane emitted, in kt
- `permeability`: Permeability, in mD
- `temperature_gradient`: Temperature gradient, in K/km
- `price_per_mass`: Price per mass, in EUR/t
- `flow`: Flow, in m3/h
- `temperature`: Temperature, in degC

Skills you can read with read_skill:
- comparing-designs: How to compare designs: a superstructure (union_designs, evolve_structure) and its front, or several families in one run_study; how to pick the design and cite the study.
- connectors: How to take a value from a connected server (MCP): call a read-only tool, cite its origin, save a series as a case file, and confirm it with the user.
- designing-a-plant: How to design a geothermal heating and cooling plant in gemini for any case: reading the case, choosing families, sizing, optimising, and what gemini can run.
- economics: How to run the uncertainty, the sensitivity and the studies of a costed design, and cite them: calls, samples and seed, failed draws, study names and keys.
- gemini-units: Units gemini accepts and returns, and how to state them.
- reading-results: How to read large results: summaries, references and `read_result`.
- report: How to quote a structure search (evolve_structure study) in the explanation: gemini's own explanation and front table, with the study key, never a number of yours.

messages.content:
## Role

You are the explainer of a verified geothermal design. You write the explanation an engineer reads:
what was built, what it delivers, what it costs, what was checked and why each major choice was
made. Every number comes from the problem state or a tool.

## Inputs

- The task from the design loop, with the reviewer's report: gemini's verdict, the changes of the
  case, a stale result and the assumptions the user has not confirmed.
- The problem state: the design (`reference`, `result`, `family`, `families`, `schematic`,
  `start_result`, `alternatives`, `study`), the verification (`result`, `failures`, `kpis`), the
  results (costs among them), the assumptions and the case.

## Tools

- `read_case`: the case of the problem state, or one section of it: the demand, the requirements
  and the economics the design was judged on.
- `case_changes`: how the case differs from the one the user gave; the user approved each change.
- `read_plant`: the design's units and their parameter values, for the capacities.
- `read_result`: a series of the verified result, such as a peak, in display units.
- `compute_kpis`: gemini's KPIs and totals of the verified result, in display units.
- `estimate_costs`: gemini's costs of the verified result, with their assumptions.
- `list_studies`: the studies stored in this chat: key, tool, method, plants, best design, and
  `current`, whether the case is still the one the study ran on.
- `read_study`: a stored study: the study file that ran, gemini's result, the designs it read and wrote.
- `search_rag`: the project's documents, when there is a project.
- `read_skill`: a skill the system prompt lists, when a rule says to read it.
- `finish`: give the explanation.

## Rules

- Read once, in one step where you can: `read_case`, `read_plant`, `compute_kpis` (without
  `names`), `estimate_costs` and `list_studies` on `design.result` and `design.reference`. What
  they gave stays in the conversation: never call them again for the same thing. The problem
  state is the `Problem state` message at the end of the conversation.

- Write only what the problem state and the tools say. Never estimate a number, never compute one,
  never round or convert it: give each number with the unit the tool returns, digit for digit
  (gemini's display units, as in the metrics below). A sum, a share or a difference you would
  need is one a tool gives, or it is left out.
- Take every reference from the problem state (`design.reference`, `design.result`,
  `verification.result`) or from `list_studies`; never make one up. A tool's `unknown_name` lists
  the references there are: take one of them, never another guess.
- Name the doublets with their depth and flows, and every unit with its capacity. Capacities come
  from `compute_kpis`'s `capacities`, in display units. `read_plant` gives the plant file's
  values in gemini's display units too (MW, degC, bar, m3/h; W/K stays W/K): quote each as it is
  given, never in another unit (#110).
- Give the heating and cooling delivered (annual) beside the demand of the case, and the peaks.
  Where delivered heat exceeds the demand, say so plainly.
- Give LCOH, LCOC, LCTS and CO2, and say which assumptions are missing or not confirmed.
- List every choice the agents made themselves (an assumption with `source: agent`), with its value
  and reason, and every change of the case the user approved, so the user can overrule them.
- List what gemini could not judge or the case does not constrain as open points. Never call the
  design compliant on those.
- Cite the study key (`study/<name>`) that each comparison, ranking, uncertainty range or choice
  relies on. `list_studies` gives the keys and says which are `current`; `read_study` gives what
  ran and what came back. Say plainly when a study ran on an older case.
- When `list_studies` shows a study of `evolve_structure` (its `tool`), read
  `read_skill('report')` before you write `Decisions`: how to quote that search.
- When `design.study` is in the state, put its ranked table (design, feasible, rank and the metrics
  with their units) under `Decisions`, and say why the best design won.
- Explain each major decision: why this family over the others, the depth and number of doublets,
  how the case's supply temperature is reached, how cooling is made, and what the optimisation
  changed from the sized start.

## Output

Finish with `finish(answer)`: Markdown with the headings `Design`, `Schematic`, `Capacities`,
`Delivered`, `Costs`, `Checks`, `Open points` and `Decisions`.

## Examples

Do and don't, from earlier runs:

- Don't ask `read_result` for a reference you made up, then six times with another `path` (#49):
  read `design.result` from the state and use it as it is.
- `compute_kpis` gave `heat_delivered` 111667.68 MWh: write `111667.68 MWh`, not `about 112 GWh`.
- `compute_kpis(names=["annualised_cost"])` is an error: costs come from `estimate_costs`.
- `read_plant` gave the heat exchanger's UA as 1500000.0 W/K: write `1500000.0 W/K`. Don't
  write `1.5 MW/K`, a conversion of your own (#110).

`## Design` then `design/<name>, family F2: one doublet with a boiler ...`, `## Delivered` then
`Heat 18.0 GWh against a demand of 18.0 GWh ...`, and so on for each heading, every number from a
tool.

## Rules for every agent

- Values: take each value from the first source that has it: the user, the project's files, the
  knowledge base (`search_rag`, `read_rag("knowledge/<name>")`), a connected server
  (`list_mcp`, `read_mcp`), and only then ask the user for the value itself. Cite each value with
  its source (file and page, document and page or row, or server, tool and time). A value no file
  or user gave enters the case or the plant only after the user confirms it. Never a typical
  value, a rule of thumb or a number you recall.
- Server answers: an origin with `future: true` is a forecast or a projection, never measured
  data: say so, and the data's dates, wherever you cite it. The case's times are UTC: a series
  from a server goes into the case as the file `save_mcp_table` writes, its times in UTC.
- No defaults: a value nothing gives stays unset and is named as missing; never fill it in.
- Units and physics: gemini converts every unit and computes every physical value. Choose the
  units you show the user, and pass values in the units their source gives; never convert a
  unit, add, multiply or derive a physical value yourself. Copy each number digit for digit.
- Findings: a `Finding` line of the problem state is a teammate's whole answer from earlier in
  this chat (a run may have stopped before its work was written). Read it with
  `read_stored(<its reference>)` and work from it; ask that teammate the same again only when the
  files or the case changed since, and say so in the brief.
- Errors: a tool error names the path, the code and the fix (`suggestions`): apply the fix, never
  repeat the same call unchanged.

## gemini's metrics

gemini's metrics, in their display units; show each with the unit gemini gives, never converted. An objective is a metric a study can minimise. Call `compute_kpis(reference)` without `names`: it gives every total and report metric it has, and a name it has not is an error. The costs (`capex`, `opex`, `annualised_cost`, `lcoh`, `lcoc`, `lcts`, `npv`, `payback`, `co2`) come from `estimate_costs`.
- `heat_delivered`: Heat delivered, in MWh
- `cold_delivered`: Cold delivered, in MWh
- `boiler_heat`: Heat from the boilers, in MWh
- `electricity_bought`: Electricity bought, in MWh
- `electricity_sold`: Electricity sold, in MWh
- `gas_bought`: Gas bought, in MWh
- `peak_heat`: Peak heat demand, in MW
- `peak_cold`: Peak cold demand, in MW
- `capex`: Investment, in MEUR
- `opex`: Operating cost, in MEUR/yr
- `annualised_cost`: Annualised cost, in MEUR/yr, objective
- `lcts`: Cost of thermal supply, in EUR/MWh, objective
- `lcoh`: Cost of heat, in EUR/MWh, objective
- `lcoc`: Cost of cold, in EUR/MWh, objective
- `annual_energy`: Energy per year, in MWh/yr
- `duration`: Duration, in d
- `analysis_period`: Analysis period, in yr
- `payback`: Payback time, in yr
- `co2`: CO2 emissions, in kt, objective
- `co2_emitted`: CO2 emitted, in kt
- `methane_emitted`: Methane emitted, in kt
- `permeability`: Permeability, in mD
- `temperature_gradient`: Temperature gradient, in K/km
- `price_per_mass`: Price per mass, in EUR/t
- `flow`: Flow, in m3/h
- `temperature`: Temperature, in degC

Skills you can read with read_skill:
- comparing-designs: How to compare designs: a superstructure (union_designs, evolve_structure) and its front, or several families in one run_study; how to pick the design and cite the study.
- connectors: How to take a value from a connected server (MCP): call a read-only tool, cite its origin, save a series as a case file, and confirm it with the user.
- designing-a-plant: How to design a geothermal heating and cooling plant in gemini for any case: reading the case, choosing families, sizing, optimising, and what gemini can run.
- economics: How to run the uncertainty, the sensitivity and the studies of a costed design, and cite them: calls, samples and seed, failed draws, study names and keys.
- gemini-units: Units gemini accepts and returns, and how to state them.
- reading-results: How to read large results: summaries, references and `read_result`.
- report: How to quote a structure search (evolve_structure study) in the explanation: gemini's own explanation and front table, with the study key, never a number of yours.

## Knowledge

`search_rag` also searches the shared knowledge base, documents such as cost catalogues, standards and reports: a match of `scope` `knowledge` has its document, title and page; `read_rag` reads a whole one as `knowledge/<document>`. A value from it is cited with its document and page, and a value that enters the case is confirmed by the user, as any value no project file gives.

Write the comparison for this request:

Goal: build and compare two complete plant configurations for the project case, then recommend one.

References to read (do not copy values, read them): the case in the problem state (sections time, site, demand, utilities, requirements, and the economics file economics.json), the demand series files GEMINI_Heating_Demand_Daily_2027.csv and GEMINI_Cooling_Demand_Daily_2027.csv, and the case requirements (doublet_count 1..3, max_production_flow 300 m3/h each, min_stable_flow 50 m3/h each, max_brine_cooling 40 °C each, pump_hydraulic_efficiency >= 0.7, volume_balance = 1, annual_operation <= 330 d, heating_supply_temperature = 100 °C, cooling_supply_temperature = 20 °C).

Family A: geothermal doublet(s) + heating supply at 100 °C + a compression chiller (electricity-driven) for the 20 °C cooling demand.
Family B: geothermal doublet(s) + heating supply at 100 °C + cooling produced from geothermal heat with an absorption chiller (geothermal-heat-driven cooling) for the 20 °C cooling demand.

For each family: build a complete configuration (all modules, all flows, all temperatures), size it, run the full 2027 year simulation (2027-01-01 to 2028-01-01, daily step), check it with GEMINI, and fix every hard-limit violation until GEMINI passes. Do not drop, relax or reinterpret any case requirement, and do not change any case value or price to make a design pass; if a case value is missing or wrong, report it as a line `case change needed: <path>: <why>` instead.

Hand back: for each family, the design reference and result reference, the GEMINI verdict (passed or the failures with their hard limits), the realised heating and cooling capacities (MW) and annual energies (MWh), electricity consumption, and the economics from the case's economics file; then a side-by-side comparison and a recommendation with the reasons, including which family meets the 20 °C cooling supply and the 100 °C heating supply and at what cost and CO2.

Do not change the case, the demand series, the requirements or the economics.

Every family:

| family | verdict | design | result | reason |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | infeasible | design/A_start |  | blocked before sizing: gemini's check of the HeatingHeatPumpCoolingPlant reports 'utilities.gas.composition is missing; expected a value in the case (it has no default)' (the class carries a gas grid, gas makeup and flare for the separated brine gas and the gas-fired peak boiler). No sizing, simulation, check or optimisation was run, so there is no result reference and no verdict on the hard limits. Case change needed: utilities.gas.composition. |
| B | infeasible | design/B_start |  | blocked before sizing: gemini's check of the HeatingAbsorptionCoolingPlant (design/B_start, built complete with params.backup='none' and params.control.dispatch='least_cost', params.control.outages='lowest_demand') reports exactly one issue, the case value 'utilities.gas.composition is missing; expected a value in the case (it has no default)'. The class carries a gas grid, gas makeup and flare for the separated brine gas and the gas-fired peak boiler, so gemini refuses to size or simulate. No sizing, simulation, check or optimisation was run, so there is no result reference and no verdict on the hard limits. Case change needed: utilities.gas.composition. |

The comparison: {}

Give the table of every family, feasible or not and why, the ranking, the Pareto set, the recommended design and why, and what was assumed. With no verified design, say so and recommend none.

## Design

Two complete configurations were built from gemini's plant classes, one per family, and both are stored:

- **Family A — `design/A_start`** (`A_compression_chiller`, class `HeatingHeatPumpCoolingPlant`): one doublet `d0` → degasser → hot filter → heat exchanger → heat pump → gas-fired peak boiler → 100 °C heating supply pipe → heating consumer; and an electricity-driven compression chiller (`compression_chiller`, a `HeatPump`) fed from the cooling return pipe, with its air cooler (`compression_cooler`), delivering the 20 °C cooling supply. Gas grid, gas makeup and flare handle the separated brine gas and the boiler fuel; electricity grid feeds the doublet, heat pump, injection pump, chiller and cooler.
- **Family B — `design/B_start`** (`B_absorption`, class `HeatingAbsorptionCoolingPlant`): one doublet `d0` → degasser → hot filter → heat exchanger → gas-fired peak boiler → drive splitter → 100 °C heating supply pipe → heating consumer; the second branch of the splitter feeds the generator of an `AbsorptionUnit` (absorption chiller), whose chilled outlet goes to the 20 °C cooling supply pipe and cooling consumer, with an air cooler (`absorption_cooler`) rejecting the condenser heat. Same gas grid / gas makeup / flare and electricity grid.

Both were built with `params.backup = 'none'` and `params.control.dispatch = 'least_cost'`, `params.control.outages = 'lowest_demand'`.

**Neither family could be sized, simulated, checked or optimised.** gemini's check of each plant against the case returns exactly one issue, the same one for both:

- `utilities.gas.composition` — `missing_value`: "utilities.gas.composition is missing; expected a value in the case (it has no default)".

The case's `utilities` section carries only `electricity.co2_intensity` (209.21 g/kWh); it has no `gas` block at all, so the gas composition of the grid gas the peak boiler burns and the makeup/flare path handle is unset. gemini refuses to size or simulate a plant whose gas path it cannot evaluate, so there is no result reference and no verdict on the hard limits for either family.

**case change needed: utilities.gas.composition: the case has no gas composition, and both plant classes carry a gas grid, gas makeup and flare for the separated brine gas and the gas-fired peak boiler; gemini's check reports it as a missing case value with no default, so neither family can be sized or simulated until the case carries it.**

## Schematic

- **A:** `d0.supply_out` → degasser → `filters.hot` → `heat_exchanger.hot_in`; `heat_exchanger.hot_out` → `heat_pump.source_in` → `filters.cold` → `injection_pump` → `d0.return_in`. Heating: `heating_return_pipe` → `heat_exchanger.cold_in` → `heat_pump.sink_in` → `peak_boiler.fluid_in` → `heating_supply_pipe` → `heating_consumer`. Cooling: `cooling_return_pipe` → `compression_chiller.source_in`, `compression_chiller.source_out` → `cooling_supply_pipe` → `cooling_consumer`; `compression_chiller.sink_out` → `compression_cooler` → back to `sink_in`. Gas: `degasser.gas_out` → `gas_makeup.gas_in`, `gas_grid` → `gas_makeup.grid_in`, `gas_makeup.fuel_out` → `peak_boiler.fuel_in`, `gas_makeup.excess_out` → `flare`.
- **B:** same brine and gas paths; heating: `heat_exchanger.cold_out` → `peak_boiler.fluid_in` → `drive_splitter.fluid_in`, `drive_splitter.branch1_out` → `heating_supply_pipe` → `heating_consumer`, `drive_splitter.branch2_out` → `absorption_chiller.generator_in`, `generator_out` → `drive_mixer.branch2_in`; `heating_return_pipe` → `drive_mixer.branch1_in` → `heat_exchanger.cold_in`. Cooling: `cooling_return_pipe` → `absorption_chiller.chilled_in`, `chilled_out` → `cooling_supply_pipe` → `cooling_consumer`; `absorption_chiller.cooling_out` → `absorption_cooler` → back to `cooling_in`.

## Capacities

None. No sizing was run for either family, so there are no realised capacities: no doublet flow, no heat-exchanger, heat-pump, boiler, compression-chiller or absorption-chiller capacity, and no pipe or pump size. `read_plant` returns no `ranges` for either design (nothing was sized), and `compute_kpis` has no result to read.

## Delivered

None. No simulation was run, so no annual heating, no annual cooling, no peak, no electricity bought or sold, no gas bought and no boiler heat exist for either family. The case's demand is the 2027 daily series `GEMINI_Heating_Demand_Daily_2027.csv` (heating, 100 °C supply / 40 °C return) and `GEMINI_Cooling_Demand_Daily_2027.csv` (cooling, 20 °C supply / 25 °C return), over 2027-01-01 to 2028-01-01 at a 1 d step; nothing was delivered against it.

## Costs

None. `estimate_costs` needs a result, and there is none for either family: no capex, opex, annualised cost, LCOH, LCOC, LCTS, NPV, payback or CO2 can be given. - **A1 — peak-boiler backup policy `none`** for both families: the boiler covers only what the doublets cannot reach, keeping the geothermal base running and sizing the fossil peak to the residual, which the case's CO2 and cost metrics reward.

- **A4 — control rules `dispatch = least_cost`, `outages = lowest_demand`**: the only values gemini's suggestions give; least_cost orders the sources by the case's prices, lowest_demand puts outages on the mildest days.
- **A5 — Family A from `HeatingHeatPumpCoolingPlant`**: the class that pairs a geothermal doublet with an electricity-driven compression chiller and a 100 °C heating supply.
- **A6 — Family B from `HeatingAbsorptionCoolingPlant`**: the class that produces the cooling from geothermal/boiler heat through an absorption chiller.
- **A7 — no project plant files, so both families from gemini's classes**: `list_plants` returned no project plants.

**Case changes the user approved: none.** `case_changes` is empty: the case is the one the user gave. The one change the design needs is the one above, `utilities.gas.composition`, and it is reported, not made.

**What the optimisation changed from the sized start: nothing.** No start design was ever sized, so there was no optimisation step and no change to report.

input.answer:
## Design

Two complete configurations were built from gemini's plant classes, one per family, and both are stored:

- **Family A — `design/A_start`** (`A_compression_chiller`, class `HeatingHeatPumpCoolingPlant`): one doublet `d0` → degasser → hot filter → heat exchanger → heat pump → gas-fired peak boiler → 100 °C heating supply pipe → heating consumer; and an electricity-driven compression chiller (`compression_chiller`, a `HeatPump`) fed from the cooling return pipe, with its air cooler (`compression_cooler`), delivering the 20 °C cooling supply. Gas grid, gas makeup and flare handle the separated brine gas and the boiler fuel; electricity grid feeds the doublet, heat pump, injection pump, chiller and cooler.
- **Family B — `design/B_start`** (`B_absorption`, class `HeatingAbsorptionCoolingPlant`): one doublet `d0` → degasser → hot filter → heat exchanger → gas-fired peak boiler → drive splitter → 100 °C heating supply pipe → heating consumer; the second branch of the splitter feeds the generator of an `AbsorptionUnit` (absorption chiller), whose chilled outlet goes to the 20 °C cooling supply pipe and cooling consumer, with an air cooler (`absorption_cooler`) rejecting the condenser heat. Same gas grid / gas makeup / flare and electricity grid.

Both were built with `params.backup = 'none'` and `params.control.dispatch = 'least_cost'`, `params.control.outages = 'lowest_demand'`.

**Neither family could be sized, simulated, checked or optimised.** gemini's check of each plant against the case returns exactly one issue, the same one for both:

- `utilities.gas.composition` — `missing_value`: "utilities.gas.composition is missing; expected a value in the case (it has no default)".

The case's `utilities` section carries only `electricity.co2_intensity` (209.21 g/kWh); it has no `gas` block at all, so the gas composition of the grid gas the peak boiler burns and the makeup/flare path handle is unset. gemini refuses to size or simulate a plant whose gas path it cannot evaluate, so there is no result reference and no verdict on the hard limits for either family.

**case change needed: utilities.gas.composition: the case has no gas composition, and both plant classes carry a gas grid, gas makeup and flare for the separated brine gas and the gas-fired peak boiler; gemini's check reports it as a missing case value with no default, so neither family can be sized or simulated until the case carries it.**

## Schematic

- **A:** `d0.supply_out` → degasser → `filters.hot` → `heat_exchanger.hot_in`; `heat_exchanger.hot_out` → `heat_pump.source_in` → `filters.cold` → `injection_pump` → `d0.return_in`. Heating: `heating_return_pipe` → `heat_exchanger.cold_in` → `heat_pump.sink_in` → `peak_boiler.fluid_in` → `heating_supply_pipe` → `heating_consumer`. Cooling: `cooling_return_pipe` → `compression_chiller.source_in`, `compression_chiller.source_out` → `cooling_supply_pipe` → `cooling_consumer`; `compression_chiller.sink_out` → `compression_cooler` → back to `sink_in`. Gas: `degasser.gas_out` → `gas_makeup.gas_in`, `gas_grid` → `gas_makeup.grid_in`, `gas_makeup.fuel_out` → `peak_boiler.fuel_in`, `gas_makeup.excess_out` → `flare`.
- **B:** same brine and gas paths; heating: `heat_exchanger.cold_out` → `peak_boiler.fluid_in` → `drive_splitter.fluid_in`, `drive_splitter.branch1_out` → `heating_supply_pipe` → `heating_consumer`, `drive_splitter.branch2_out` → `absorption_chiller.generator_in`, `generator_out` → `drive_mixer.branch2_in`; `heating_return_pipe` → `drive_mixer.branch1_in` → `heat_exchanger.cold_in`. Cooling: `cooling_return_pipe` → `absorption_chiller.chilled_in`, `chilled_out` → `cooling_supply_pipe` → `cooling_consumer`; `absorption_chiller.cooling_out` → `absorption_cooler` → back to `cooling_in`.

## Capacities

None. No sizing was run for either family, so there are no realised capacities: no doublet flow, no heat-exchanger, heat-pump, boiler, compression-chiller or absorption-chiller capacity, and no pipe or pump size. `read_plant` returns no `ranges` for either design (nothing was sized), and `compute_kpis` has no result to read.

## Delivered

None. No simulation was run, so no annual heating, no annual cooling, no peak, no electricity bought or sold, no gas bought and no boiler heat exist for either family. The case's demand is the 2027 daily series `GEMINI_Heating_Demand_Daily_2027.csv` (heating, 100 °C supply / 40 °C return) and `GEMINI_Cooling_Demand_Daily_2027.csv` (cooling, 20 °C supply / 25 °C return), over 2027-01-01 to 2028-01-01 at a 1 d step; nothing was delivered against it.

## Costs

None. `estimate_costs` needs a result, and there is none for either family: no capex, opex, annualised cost, LCOH, LCOC, LCTS, NPV, payback or CO2 can be given. The economics file the designs would be judged on is present and complete for its part — discount rate 0.051, analysis period 25 yr, electricity 115.01546759736655 EUR/MWh, heat revenue 114.555 EUR/MWh, cold revenue 103.547 EUR/MWh, carbon price 57.4757281553398 EUR/t, heat cost share 0.76, GWP CH4 27.9 (IPCC AR6 GWP100), price year 2015 — but no cost was computed on it.

## Checks

| family | verdict | design | result | reason |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | infeasible | design/A_start | — | blocked before sizing: gemini's check of the `HeatingHeatPumpCoolingPlant` reports `utilities.gas.composition` missing with no default. No sizing, simulation, check or optimisation was run, so there is no result reference and no verdict on the hard limits. Case change needed: `utilities.gas.composition`. |
| B | infeasible | design/B_start | — | blocked before sizing: gemini's check of the `HeatingAbsorptionCoolingPlant` reports exactly the same single issue, `utilities.gas.composition` missing with no default. No sizing, simulation, check or optimisation was run, so there is no result reference and no verdict on the hard limits. Case change needed: `utilities.gas.composition`. |

No requirement of the case was dropped, relaxed or reinterpreted, and no case value, price or demand series was changed. The nine requirements (R1 doublet_count 1..3, R2 max_production_flow 300 m3/h each, R3 min_stable_flow 50 m3/h each, R4 max_brine_cooling 40 °C each, R5 pump_hydraulic_efficiency ≥ 0.7, R6 volume_balance = 1, R7 annual_operation ≤ 330 d, R8 heating_supply_temperature = 100 °C, R9 cooling_supply_temperature = 20 °C) all remain **open**: nothing was simulated, so none of them was tested.

## Open points

- **`utilities.gas.composition` is missing from the case** and is the single blocker for both families. Until the user supplies it (or confirms a value from a document), neither family can be sized, simulated or checked, and no requirement can be judged.
- **Nothing is known about the hard limits.** Whether the doublet count, the 300 m3/h maximum and 50 m3/h minimum flow, the 40 °C maximum brine cooling, the 0.7 pump efficiency, the volume balance of 1, the 330 d operation limit, the 100 °C heating supply and the 20 °C cooling supply are met is untested for both families. Neither family can be called compliant.
- **Which family meets the 20 °C cooling supply and the 100 °C heating supply, and at what cost and CO2, is undetermined.** Both configurations are wired to deliver those temperatures (A through the compression chiller and the heat pump plus peak boiler; B through the absorption chiller and the peak boiler), but no simulation shows it.
- **No study exists.** `list_studies` is empty: no `run_study`, no `optimize`, no uncertainty or sensitivity study was run, so there is no study key to cite for any comparison, ranking or range, and no Pareto front.
- **No project plant files exist**; both families come from gemini's plant classes, so no project-specific equipment data constrains them.
- The economics file's cost entries carry their own `status` in `about.sources` (several `secondary`), and the case's `utilities` has no gas price at all — a gas-fired peak boiler has no fuel price to cost against, which will matter once the gas composition is supplied.

## Decisions

**Ranking: none.** With no verified design there is nothing to rank. Both families are infeasible at the same point and for the same reason, so they are tied at "not evaluated", not ordered.

**Pareto set: empty.** No design has a cost or a CO2 value, so no front exists.

**Recommended design: none.** I recommend no family. The request cannot be answered as posed until the case carries `utilities.gas.composition`; choosing between a compression chiller and an absorption chiller on cost and CO2 without a single simulated hour would be a guess, not a comparison.

**Why each family was built the way it was** (the choices the agents made themselves, all unconfirmed, for the user to overrule):

- **A1 — peak-boiler backup policy `none`** for both families: the boiler covers only what the doublets cannot reach, keeping the geothermal base running and sizing the fossil peak to the residual, which the case's CO2 and cost metrics reward.
- **A2 — search objective `lcts`** (levelised cost of thermal supply, heating plus cooling): the case serves two energy carriers, so a combined levelised cost is the single metric that ranks them.
- **A3 — search budget 30 evaluations, seed 0**: fits the search time limit on a plant with a handful of ranges.
- **A4 — control rules `dispatch = least_cost`, `outages = lowest_demand`**: the only values gemini's suggestions give; least_cost orders the sources by the case's prices, lowest_demand puts outages on the mildest days.
- **A5 — Family A from `HeatingHeatPumpCoolingPlant`**: the class that pairs a geothermal doublet with an electricity-driven compression chiller and a 100 °C heating supply.
- **A6 — Family B from `HeatingAbsorptionCoolingPlant`**: the class that produces the cooling from geothermal/boiler heat through an absorption chiller.
- **A7 — no project plant files, so both families from gemini's classes**: `list_plants` returned no project plants.

**Case changes the user approved: none.** `case_changes` is empty: the case is the one the user gave. The one change the design needs is the one above, `utilities.gas.composition`, and it is reported, not made.

**What the optimisation changed from the sized start: nothing.** No start design was ever sized, so there was no optimisation step and no change to report.
